sections.title: Reading Comprehension · Passage B
sections.intro: Read “Slam, Dunk, & Hook” and answer questions 10–14. Vocabulary notes follow the poem.

passage.title: Slam, Dunk, & Hook
passage.credit: —Yusef Komunyakaa · “Slam, Dunk, & Hook,” from Pleasure Dome: New and Collected Poems (2004), Wesleyan University Press

lines.text: Fast breaks. Lay ups. With Mercury’s¹
Of bad angels. Nothing but a hot
Ten feet out. In the roundhouse
He played nonstop all day, so hard
We had moves we didn’t know
Of joy, & we knew we were
¹ Mercury — Roman god who acted as a messenger to the gods

questions.prompt: The images in lines 6 through 12 create a sense of
questions.explanation: The players seem to “last forever” while poised in midair, and a note hangs for “a long second.” These suspended images make a basketball moment feel as if time has stopped.

questions.prompt: In the context of the poem as a whole, lines 24 through 26 present

choices.text: an example of the players’ excitement with the game
a shift in the players’ expectations
a contrast to the players’ feelings of invincibility
an illustration of the players’ skill

questions.explanation: The poem otherwise portrays the players as almost superhuman and full of joy. Sonny Boy’s mother’s death brings real grief into that exhilaration, reminding us they are not invincible.

questions.prompt: Lines 32 through 36 most clearly reflect the players’
questions.explanation: The players dribble, drive, glide, and spin with surprising moves. These verbs emphasize their quick, graceful physical agility.

questions.prompt: In the context of the poem as a whole, the mythological allusions best reflect the players’ sense of being
questions.explanation: Mercury, angels, sea monsters, and the description “metaphysical” make the players seem beyond ordinary humans. The allusions convey their sense of being extraordinary.

questions.prompt: Which quotation best reflects a central idea of the poem?

choices.text: “We’d corkscrew / Up & dunk balls that exploded” (lines 13 and 14)
“We were metaphysical when girls / Cheered on the sidelines” (lines 18 and 19)
“Glistening with sweat / We rolled the ball off / Our fingertips” (lines 27 through 29)
“Of joy, & we knew we were / Beautiful & dangerous” (lines 39 and 40)

questions.explanation: The final lines sum up the poem’s portrayal of basketball as shared joy and an exhilarating sense of beauty and power. The other quotations show individual moments of play.
